title: Kohli's 74 Steers India to Five-Wicket DLS Win Over New Zealand in Auckland Opener
excerpt: India seamers bowled New Zealand out for 185 at Eden Park, and Virat Kohli 74 off 51 balls carried the chase of a rain-revised 143 in 32 overs, finished with 56 balls to spare. India lead the five-match series 1-0.
body:
• India beat New Zealand by five wickets under the DLS method in the rain-hit first ODI at Eden Park, Auckland, on Wednesday, to lead the five-match series 1-0.
  • New Zealand were bowled out for 185 in 40.2 overs: Arshdeep Singh took 4 for 70, Gurnoor Brar 3 for 44, and Anshul Kamboj — Player of the Match — conceded only 22 runs in his 10 overs for two wickets.
  • Set a revised target of 143 in 32 overs after two rain interruptions, India finished on 143 for 5 in 22.4 overs, with Virat Kohli 74 off 51 balls (13 fours, one six) settling the chase.
  • It was New Zealand first defeat in the opening match of a home ODI series in 12 series, according to Cricbuzz.

India young pace attack set the match up and Virat Kohli finished it. Bowling first after winning the toss at Eden Park, India dismissed New Zealand for 185 in 40.2 overs, then chased a DLS-revised target of 143 from 32 overs with 56 balls to spare, reaching 143 for 5 in 22.4 overs, according to ESPNcricinfo. The win gives India a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.

Seamers first: 185 all out

Arshdeep Singh struck early, removing Will Young and Henry Nicholls for 9 apiece inside the first ten overs, and returned to finish with 4 for 70. The pick of the attack, though, was Anshul Kamboj, chosen ahead of Mohammed Siraj: he extracted seam movement into his last over, conceded just 22 runs in 10 overs with two maidens, and took the wickets of captain Mitchell Santner and Nathan Smith on his way to the Player of the Match award, ESPNcricinfo reported. Gurnoor Brar took 3 for 44, ending a 39-run last-wicket stand in which Blair Tickner hit 34 off 23 balls. Tim Seifert top-scored for New Zealand with 38; without the tail stand, the hosts would have finished well below 185.

Rain, a revised target, and Kohli

The chase was interrupted twice by rain and eventually cut to 32 overs, with India target set at 143. Rohit Sharma fell for a six-ball duck, but Kohli took the chase away from New Zealand: he reached his fifty off 35 balls with a pull through mid-wicket and finished with 74 off 51 balls, including 13 fours and a six, before Jacob Duffy had him caught by Seifert at deep backward square leg in the 20th over. Shubman Gill made 37, and India crossed the line three overs later. Duffy was New Zealand best bowler with 3 for 49.

Kohli innings came a day before his 38th birthday, and it carried the weight the pre-series coverage expected of him: India build-up had centred on his form and milestones, and on a tricky, rain-shortened surface his scoring rate — 145 runs per hundred balls — was, as Cricbuzz put it, much of the difference between the sides.

What it means

India lead 1-0 with four matches to play, and the selection questions that opened the series have early answers: Kamboj justified his place ahead of Siraj, and the three-man seam attack of Arshdeep, Brar and Kamboj took nine of the ten wickets. For New Zealand, a first opening-match defeat in a home ODI series in 12 series, per Cricbuzz, leaves them needing a response in the second match of the series.
